newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: IMI Sigeco says OMV overvalued, "sell".
newsitem.headline: IMI Sigeco says OMV overvalued, "sell".

text.p: London-based brokers IMI Sigeco rates Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV AG a "sell" on the view that the company is still structurally unbalanced and the shares are overvalued at current levels.
"It appears that the expected growth is already in the price and the company is currently overvalued", IMI Sigeco said in a research report obtained on Friday.

IMI Sigeco expects earnings per share to rise to 99 schillings in 1998 against a forecast 71 schillings in 1997. In 1999, earnings per share are seen to grow to 115 schillings and in 2000 to 130 schillings.
IMI Sigeco's discounted cash-flow model provides a motivated share price of around 1,030 schillings, "some 30 percent lower than the current market price".
Furthermore, IMI Sigeco considers OMV still a structurally unbalanced company with significantly higher exposure to the downstream and petrochemicals businesses than most of its competitors.

"Whereas the average integrated oil company has a 60/30/10 division of total investments between upstream, downstream and chemicals, respectively, OMV is close to having one-third of its investments in each of these sectors", IMI Sigeco notes.

New production coming onstream and OMV's presence in the lucrative gas transportation business are not considered sufficient compensation for the exposure to the low margin downstream activities and the large and volatile chemicals and plastics businesses.
IMI Sigeco views the lack of genuine growth prospects for OMV's petrochemical divisions as a major long-term problem for the group.

"Unless we will see continued heavy restructuring, which will be costly in the short term, future earnings development in the chemicals and plastics divisions will be driven more by the volatile market conditions rather than by internal work", IMI Sigeco said.
